title: Reduce consumer rebalance latency and introduce graceful worker eviction
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem summary:

Several recent incidents and load tests show long Kafka consumer-group rebalances and abrupt worker restarts cause a large number of in-flight jobs to be retried, often doubling downstream load and rapidly exhausting retry budgets. Symptoms: high tail latency during rebalances, duplicate work for idempotent-but-costly tasks (embedding uploads, external HTTP calls), spike in errors from downstream services, and noisy autoscaling triggers.

Root causes observed: cooperative-sticky assignment mismatches, long shutdown hooks that don't drain in-flight tasks, missing pre-stop drain semantics in our Docker images, and the current retry mechanism immediately re-enqueues jobs without upstream backpressure signals or worker-eviction coordination. Redis-based lease checks are racing with consumer group changes which can leave orphaned leases.

Goal: reduce mean and tail rebalance latency by ~50% in our largest topics, and implement a graceful eviction path so workers leaving a group hand off in-flight partitions/jobs to a small number of warm standby workers without generating mass retries. This should reduce transient downstream error spikes and improve SLA stability during scaling or deployments.
acceptance_criteria: Average consumer-group rebalance time for topic 'inference-requests' reduced by >=50% under 50k partitions workload in staging
No more than 5% increase in retried jobs during a controlled rolling restart canary compared to normal baseline
Linked dashboards show rebalance count, rebalance duration, in-flight job counts during drain, and retry-burst rate
Graceful eviction implemented: pre-stop drain completes handoff in >90% of canary restarts within configured grace window
E2E test added that simulates concurrent rebalances + worker restarts and asserts no duplicate external POSTs beyond idempotency-safe retries
design_decisions: Prefer cooperative-sticky consumer protocol and tune 'max.poll.interval.ms' and heartbeat settings rather than full reassignments when possible
Add explicit pre-stop drain hook to the worker Docker image which sets 'leaving' state in Redis and waits for in-flight tasks to complete or be gracefully handed off
Introduce a lightweight lease-transfer protocol stored in Redis hash (lease key -> candidate list) to allow another worker to immediately claim ownership without re-enqueueing
Change retry semantics so that when a worker is evicting it marks tasks as 'handoff-in-progress' with short TTL and not immediate requeue; only fallback to standard retry after TTL expires
Expose a backpressure signal via our internal request router (HTTP 429 + X-Redwood-Backpressure headers) when consumer pool saturation is detected
Keep changes backward-compatible: fall back to current behavior via config flags for canary groups
migration_plan: Phase 1: Unit + integration tests for lease-transfer and drain hooks (local CI)
Phase 2: Canary consumer group in staging: enable cooperative-sticky + heartbeat tuning on 10% of consumers, monitor rebalance metrics for 48h
Phase 3: Deploy pre-stop drain image to canary workers and run rolling restarts on staging topics, validate no retry spikes
Phase 4: Enable Redis lease-transfer and handoff semantics for canary, run chaos tests (kill 1/3rd of workers quickly)
Phase 5: Gradual rollout to prod with feature-flag gating per cluster and post-release monitoring for 7 days
implementation_tasks: Add 'leaving' state and handoff protocol to worker runtime (worker/lease_manager.go)
Implement pre-stop drain script in container ENTRYPOINT and add to Dockerfile
Instrument metrics: rebalance_duration_ms, handoff_success_rate, handoff_latency_ms, retry_burst_count
Router: implement X-Redwood-Backpressure header and 429 logic when worker pool queued length > threshold
E2E test harness: extend kafka-sim test container to simulate cooperative rebalances and verify idempotent external calls
Create dashboards and alerts in Grafana/Datadog tied to rebalance_duration_ms and handoff_success_rate
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Lease-transfer races under network partition. Mitigation: use short TTLs + compare-and-set on Redis keys and a last-writer-wins timestamp, plus fall back to requeue if transfer fails
Risk: Backpressure header may not be honored by older services. Mitigation: conservative rollout and provide router-side local shedding as fallback
Risk: Longer graceful-drain windows could delay deploys. Mitigation: configurable grace window per environment and an emergency 'force-evict' flag for urgent rollouts
